entrypoints.summary: DatabaseCLI.serve reads newline-terminated hex input, decodes it as UTF-8, and dispatches add, get, or auth requests; the container exposes the process through TCP port 1337.
The official trigger is an unauthenticated add request with outer key x and a CR-bearing value that injects secret_password:x after decoding.

affected_components.role: LF-only persistence validation and text-mode record parsing
hex transport, secret-prefix authorization, final-password selection, and protected-flag initialization

code_slices.surrounding_context: DatabaseCLI permits unauthenticated non-secret outer keys, validates against the final secret_password history entry, and conditionally permits secret_-prefixed get requests after auth.
code_slices.vulnerable: TextDatabase.add rejects '\n' but not '\r' in value and appends key:value plus '\n'; TextDatabase.get iterates text-mode lines and splits each at ':'.

negative_controls: An unprivileged direct get of a secret_-prefixed key is denied by the request handler.
No supplied artifact records an actual run of either control.
observability.positive_marker: An authorized protected get returns retrieved values in an ok: get response, which contains the initialized secret_flag.

preconditions: The CLI is reachable through its line-oriented hex input channel.
The attacker can submit an unauthenticated add whose outer key does not start with secret_.
Python text-mode universal-newline behavior is used by the database reader.

trigger_steps.summary: Hex-encode and submit the documented add request with outer key x and a value containing CR followed by secret_password:x.
Authenticate using x and issue a nested request for secret_flag.

relation_candidates.rationale: The accepted CR survives LF-only validation and is later interpreted as a logical record boundary, yielding a synthetic secret_password record.
The password validator selects the last secret_password value, allowing the injected x value to become the authentication value.
A successful auth request authorizes a nested protected get, and the challenge initializes secret_flag in the database.

Rejecting all newline separators recognized by the reader, or using one canonical serialization/parser grammar, prevents an accepted value from becoming an extra record. This is an inferred remediation, not a supplied patch.

impact.affected_asset: The secret password state and the stored flag protected by the secret_ authorization prefix.
impact.attacker_capability: An unauthenticated client can create a synthetic secret_password record with a chosen final password, authenticate using that password, and request secret_flag.
impact.security_effect: Authentication-state overwrite followed by disclosure of a protected database value.

causal_trace.summary: An unauthenticated client can hex-encode a request whose decoded add value contains carriage return; the documented example is add x x followed by CR and secret_password:x.

Authorization considers only outer key x non-secret, while TextDatabase.add rejects LF in values but not CR and persists key:value plus LF. Thus accepted input is not constrained to one logical record under the reader's newline language.

TextDatabase.get opens the file in Python text mode and iterates lines before splitting each line at the first colon. Python universal-newline handling treats the injected CR as a line boundary, causing the persisted add to parse as a separate secret_password:x record.

Password validation retrieves password history and compares against its final value, so the synthetic final secret_password:x entry permits auth x; an authorized get can then retrieve the preloaded secret_flag value.

failure.operation: Python text-mode line iteration splits a CR-containing stored value into an additional parsed key/value record.

primary_invariant.statement: Every accepted add operation must serialize to exactly one logical key/value record when later enumerated by TextDatabase.get, and unprivileged input must not create a secret_-prefixed record.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The write validator excludes LF but permits CR, whereas the text-mode reader recognizes CR as a newline boundary.

quality.review_notes: Official writeup, complete challenge source, and runtime definition substantiate the causal chain. No corrective patch, regression test, or captured execution result is supplied; the verification oracle is a source-defined contract, not evidence that a vulnerable or fixed test was run. This is deliberately vulnerable CTF code, not evidence of a production deployment flaw.

remediation.invariant_restored: No accepted key or value can introduce any separator recognized by the reader, so one successful add remains one parsed record and cannot synthesize a secret_-prefixed record.
mitigation_classes: reject carriage-return and line-feed record separators before line-delimited persistence
use a serialization and parser pair with one canonical record-boundary grammar

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker submits a newline-delimited hex transport record that decodes to the documented CR-bearing add request; no prior authorization is required because outer key x is not secret-prefixed.
data_structure_invariants: Each physical appended entry must map to one logical record during retrieval.
Only authorized requests may create or retrieve secret_-prefixed records.
The last secret_password record determines password validation.
state_context.state_machine: Unauthenticated add of a non-secret outer key -> persistence of CR-bearing value -> later text-mode parse creates final secret_password entry -> auth with injected password -> authorized protected get.

oracle.channel: hex-encoded stdin request and hex-encoded CLI response
oracle.expected_negative: A record-boundary-safe implementation rejects or safely encodes CR-bearing input so the chosen injected password does not become the final secret_password value.
oracle.expected_positive: After the CR-bearing unauthenticated add, auth with the injected chosen password can authorize a protected get and expose the stored secret_flag value.
